title: Asians can get big TOO!
summary: NH attacks the blackpill belief that Asian (and Indian) men are genetically doomed to be small and weak, tracing the 'sick man of Asia' stereotype to colonial history and arguing it is now mostly self-inflicted. He prescribes lifting or martial arts as the cure, drawing on Bruce Lee, Mas Oyama's mottos, Tommy Kono, old-school Indian bodybuilders and modern natural Asian bodybuilders.
claims: Blackpill demoralization, the idea that you are doomed at birth, is the plague of the century and must be fought
Asian men online seem to have it worst: a common belief says being born Asian dooms you to weakness and small muscles no matter how hard you train

He traces Asian self-limiting beliefs to the 'sick man of Asia' trope born from colonial defeats starting with the Opium Wars; historical samurai and Chinese generals saw themselves as superior, not inferior
The modern online slur 'bugmen' is the same stereotype rebranded, and Asians themselves now spread it, having internalized the lie
Much of the hate aimed at Asian men, like hate aimed at short men, comes from within the group itself: self-hatred that accepts and amplifies stereotypes
Words cannot convince you that you are not weak; you have to prove it to yourself, and the best way is to build your body by lifting or doing martial arts
Essentially all Asian men who believe they are destined to stay small and weak have never seriously tried to improve; those who tried know it is a lie
Mas Oyama's motto: progress is like scaling a cliff with no rest; those who quit never prove their worth and convince themselves they never had what it takes
Take the initiative in all things; the stereotype of the passive, meek, herbivorous Asian man stunts social skills and self-development
Respect is a virtue but you need not be respectful to people who do not respect you; stand tall rather than letting people walk over you
Anecdote: growing up in Paris's Chinese district he saw meek Asian friends let others take their money and food to seem nice
Strength is always the solution in life; the pain of changing yourself lasts months or years while the pain of staying weak lasts forever
Confidence is the main thing missing from the Asian men he meets; reclaiming pride brings confidence and confident people can be grateful
The blackpill feeds on passivity and is destroyed by action; complaining changes nothing
Indian men should take old-school Indian bodybuilders as role models over Bollywood actors on PEDs; those men were mostly vegetarian, had almost no equipment and still built great physiques
Claims that this generation is doomed by plastics in food and crushed testosterone are excuses people use to explain why they suck
Tommy Kono, born frail and asthmatic and interned in a WWII camp, turned to weightlifting and bodybuilding and became a champion: proof against self-limiting beliefs
Asian lifters often gravitate to calisthenics and skill work because they assume they cannot get big; that is still a self-limiting belief, they can pursue a big physique too
Natural Asian bodybuilders like Eugene Teo on YouTube disprove the claim that Asian men have bad bodybuilding genetics
He thinks Asian men often have good bodybuilding genetics: great flow, huge legs, good core aesthetics and good shoulder width; being shorter is an advantage since bodybuilding favors short men
If you see your genetics as a weakness it becomes one; potential is worthless until you put in the work
